1	---
2	name: incident-sync
3	description: Turn one Grafana Notification into Incident activity in the Jira OPS project.
4	---
5	
6	# One Notification, one Incident lifecycle
7	
8	Read `notification.json` in your working directory. Handle **every Alert in it
9	independently**: an Alert is `firing` or `resolved`, and its `fingerprint` is its
10	identity across every Notification it ever appears in.
11	
12	You can run `jira-as` and read files. Nothing else — no writing files, no `curl`,
13	no `date`, no other command. Every invocation below is one you can run as written.
14	
15	**Write each `jira-as` invocation on a single line, in plain single quotes.** The
16	permission boundary denies a whole command that is split across lines with `\`,
17	that carries a newline inside an argument, or that uses `$'...'` — it will not
18	match the allow list however harmless it looks. Nothing you need has a newline in
19	it: the one field that wants paragraphs is the Description, and it gets them from
20	the ADF form below instead.
21	
22	## The project
23	
24	| Fact | Value |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| Project | `OPS` |
27	| Issue type | `Incident` |
28	| Fingerprint label | `fp-<fingerprint>` — nothing else identifies an Incident |
29	| Severity field | `customfield_10085`, one of `Sev-1`, `Sev-2`, `Sev-3` |
30	| Urgency field | `customfield_10079`, one of `Critical`, `High`, `Medium` |
31	| Source field | `customfield_10096`, always `Monitoring systems` |
32	
33	Never set `Sev-0`. Never touch Major incident (`customfield_10083`). Never use the
34	statuses `Pending`, `Closed` or `Canceled` — a human owns those.
35	
36	## Step 1 — find the Match
37	
38	The Match is the one open Incident carrying this Alert's Fingerprint label:
39	
40	```bash
41	jira-as search jql 'project = OPS AND issuetype = Incident AND labels = "fp-<fingerprint>" AND statusCategory != Done'
42	```
43	
44	`Found 0 issue(s)` means there is no Match. Otherwise the table's `Key` column is
45	the Match and its `Status` is what the next step branches on. A Completed Incident
46	is deliberately not a Match: a re-fire gets its own Incident.
47	
48	Then act on what you found:
49	
50	| Alert | Match | What you do |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| `firing` | none | [Create](#step-2a--create-the-incident) it |
53	| `firing` | `Open` | [Comment](#step-2b--comment-the-trend) the trend, then move it to `Work in progress` |
54	| `firing` | `Work in progress` | [Comment](#step-2b--comment-the-trend) the trend and nothing else |
55	| `resolved` | any | [Close](#step-2c--close-the-incident) it |
56	| `resolved` | none | Do nothing. Say you skipped it and why |
57	
58	## Step 2a — create the Incident
59	
60	Map the Alert onto the fields:
61	
62	- **Summary** — the `alertname` label, then ` on `, then the `instance` label.
63	- **Description** — the `summary` annotation, then the `description` annotation,
64	  then the Alert's `generatorURL`, `dashboardURL` and `panelURL`, one per line.
65	  Written as ADF, because that is the only way to get separate lines out of a
66	  command that cannot contain one. See [the template](#the-description) below.
67	- **Severity** — `critical` → `Sev-1`, `warning` → `Sev-2`, anything else → `Sev-3`,
68	  read from the `severity` label.
69	- **Urgency** — follows Severity: `Sev-1` → `Critical`, `Sev-2` → `High`,
70	  `Sev-3` → `Medium`.
71	- **Component** — the `service` label, but only if a component of that exact name
72	  already exists on OPS. Check with
73	  `jira-as -o json api call getProjectComponents --projectIdOrKey OPS`. If it is
74	  not there, leave the component off entirely. An unknown service must not fail
75	  the create.
76	- **Label** — `fp-<fingerprint>`, and no other label.
77	
78	```bash
79	jira-as issue create -p OPS -t Incident -s '<summary>' --labels 'fp-<fingerprint>' --custom-fields '{"customfield_10085": {"value": "Sev-1"}, "customfield_10079": {"value": "Critical"}, "customfield_10096": {"value": "Monitoring systems"}, "description": <description>}'
80	```
81	
82	Add `--components '<service>'` only when that component exists. The Incident is
83	created in `Open`; do not transition it on the first Firing.
84	
85	Then record the value it opened at, so the next Firing has something to compare
86	against and the closing comment can count the Firings:
87	
88	```bash
89	jira-as collaborate comment add <key> -b 'Opened from a firing Alert. value=<current>.'
90	```
91	
92	`<current>` is the Alert's `values.A`.
93	
94	### The description
95	
96	The Description goes in under `--custom-fields` with the other fields, as one
97	line of ADF JSON — `issue create` has no `--description` that understands
98	paragraphs, and a command may not contain a newline. Fill in the five
99	placeholders, change nothing else, and paste it in place of `<description>`
100	above, unquoted, as a JSON value among the others:
101	
102	```json
103	{"type":"doc","version":1,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<summary annotation>"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<description annotation>"}]},{"type":"bulletList","content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Generator: <generatorURL>"}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Dashboard: <dashboardURL>"}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Panel: <panelURL>"}]}]}]}]}
104	```
105	
106	## Step 2b — comment the trend
107	
108	Read what the last Run said, so this comment can report a change:
109	
110	```bash
111	jira-as collaborate comment list <key>
112	```
113	
114	The most recent `value=` in that list is the previous value. Then post one comment
115	and no more than one, in exactly this shape, so the next Run can read it too:
116	
117	```bash
118	jira-as collaborate comment add <key> -b 'Still firing. value=<current> (previous value=<previous>, <up|down|unchanged>). Open for <duration>.'
119	```
120	
121	`<duration>` is how long the Incident has been open: the Jira clock now, minus
122	the Incident's own `created`. Read both off Jira, never off the Alert — Grafana's
123	clock and Jira's are not the same clock, and a Notification replayed from a
124	fixture can carry a `startsAt` that has not happened yet:
125	
126	```bash
127	jira-as -o json api call getServerInfo
128	jira-as issue get <key> -o json
129	```
130	
131	`serverTime` from the first, `created` from the second. Write the difference like
132	`4m30s`. That is the only clock you can reach, so use it for every duration.
133	
134	If the Match is in `Open`, move it on after commenting — see
135	[transitions](#moving-an-incident). If it is already in `Work in progress`, stop
136	here: a repeat is idempotent apart from its comment.
137	
138	## Step 2c — close the Incident
139	
140	Count the Firings: every comment on the Incident carrying a `value=` is one, the
141	opening one included. The duration is the Jira clock now minus the Incident's
142	`created`, read the same way as in [step 2b](#step-2b--comment-the-trend).
143	
144	```bash
145	jira-as collaborate comment add <key> -b 'Resolved after <duration>, <n> Firings. value=<current>. Completed automatically from the Grafana Alert.'
146	```
147	
148	Then move it to `Completed` **with a resolution**:
149	
150	```bash
151	jira-as lifecycle transition <key> --id <id> --resolution Done
152	```
153	
154	Without the resolution the Incident stays in the Incidents queue forever, because
155	that queue is `resolution = Unresolved`. This is the one place a resolution is set.
156	
157	## Moving an Incident
158	
159	Transition names are not status names on this workflow: `Investigate` leads to
160	`Work in progress` and `Resolve` leads to `Completed`. So never pass `--to`. Read
161	the transitions off the issue itself and use the id of the one whose `to.name` is
162	the status you want:
163	
164	```bash
165	jira-as lifecycle transitions <key> -o json
166	jira-as lifecycle transition <key> --id <id>
167	```
168	
169	Read them every time. An id that was right last week is not a fact about this issue.
170	
171	## Finish
172	
173	End with one line per Alert, naming the Fingerprint, the Incident key and what
174	changed — `created`, `commented`, `commented and moved to Work in progress`,
175	`completed`, or `skipped` and why. Nothing else after those lines.
176

---
name: incident-sync
description: Turn one Grafana Notification into Incident activity in the Jira OPS project.
---

# One Notification, one Incident lifecycle

Read `notification.json` in your working directory. Handle **every Alert in it
independently**: an Alert is `firing` or `resolved`, and its `fingerprint` is its
identity across every Notification it ever appears in.

You can run `jira-as` and read files. Nothing else — no writing files, no `curl`,
no `date`, no other command. Every invocation below is one you can run as written.

**Write each `jira-as` invocation on a single line, in plain single quotes.** The
permission boundary denies a whole command that is split across lines with `\`,
that carries a newline inside an argument, or that uses `$'...'` — it will not
match the allow list however harmless it looks. Nothing you need has a newline in
it: the one field that wants paragraphs is the Description, and it gets them from
the ADF form below instead.

## The project

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Project | `OPS` |
| Issue type | `Incident` |
| Fingerprint label | `fp-<fingerprint>` — nothing else identifies an Incident |
| Severity field | `customfield_10085`, one of `Sev-1`, `Sev-2`, `Sev-3` |
| Urgency field | `customfield_10079`, one of `Critical`, `High`, `Medium` |
| Source field | `customfield_10096`, always `Monitoring systems` |

Never set `Sev-0`. Never touch Major incident (`customfield_10083`). Never use the
statuses `Pending`, `Closed` or `Canceled` — a human owns those.

## Step 1 — find the Match

The Match is the one open Incident carrying this Alert's Fingerprint label:

```bash
jira-as search jql 'project = OPS AND issuetype = Incident AND labels = "fp-<fingerprint>" AND statusCategory != Done'
```

`Found 0 issue(s)` means there is no Match. Otherwise the table's `Key` column is
the Match and its `Status` is what the next step branches on. A Completed Incident
is deliberately not a Match: a re-fire gets its own Incident.

Then act on what you found:

| Alert | Match | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `firing` | none | [Create](#step-2a--create-the-incident) it |
| `firing` | `Open` | [Comment](#step-2b--comment-the-trend) the trend, then move it to `Work in progress` |
| `firing` | `Work in progress` | [Comment](#step-2b--comment-the-trend) the trend and nothing else |
| `resolved` | any | [Close](#step-2c--close-the-incident) it |
| `resolved` | none | Do nothing. Say you skipped it and why |

## Step 2a — create the Incident

Map the Alert onto the fields:

- **Summary** — the `alertname` label, then ` on `, then the `instance` label.
- **Description** — the `summary` annotation, then the `description` annotation,
  then the Alert's `generatorURL`, `dashboardURL` and `panelURL`, one per line.
  Written as ADF, because that is the only way to get separate lines out of a
  command that cannot contain one. See [the template](#the-description) below.
- **Severity** — `critical` → `Sev-1`, `warning` → `Sev-2`, anything else → `Sev-3`,
  read from the `severity` label.
- **Urgency** — follows Severity: `Sev-1` → `Critical`, `Sev-2` → `High`,
  `Sev-3` → `Medium`.
- **Component** — the `service` label, but only if a component of that exact name
  already exists on OPS. Check with
  `jira-as -o json api call getProjectComponents --projectIdOrKey OPS`. If it is
  not there, leave the component off entirely. An unknown service must not fail
  the create.
- **Label** — `fp-<fingerprint>`, and no other label.

```bash
jira-as issue create -p OPS -t Incident -s '<summary>' --labels 'fp-<fingerprint>' --custom-fields '{"customfield_10085": {"value": "Sev-1"}, "customfield_10079": {"value": "Critical"}, "customfield_10096": {"value": "Monitoring systems"}, "description": <description>}'
```

Add `--components '<service>'` only when that component exists. The Incident is
created in `Open`; do not transition it on the first Firing.

Then record the value it opened at, so the next Firing has something to compare
against and the closing comment can count the Firings:

```bash
jira-as collaborate comment add <key> -b 'Opened from a firing Alert. value=<current>.'
```

`<current>` is the Alert's `values.A`.

### The description

The Description goes in under `--custom-fields` with the other fields, as one
line of ADF JSON — `issue create` has no `--description` that understands
paragraphs, and a command may not contain a newline. Fill in the five
placeholders, change nothing else, and paste it in place of `<description>`
above, unquoted, as a JSON value among the others:

```json
{"type":"doc","version":1,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<summary annotation>"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<description annotation>"}]},{"type":"bulletList","content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Generator: <generatorURL>"}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Dashboard: <dashboardURL>"}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Panel: <panelURL>"}]}]}]}]}
```

## Step 2b — comment the trend

Read what the last Run said, so this comment can report a change:

```bash
jira-as collaborate comment list <key>
```

The most recent `value=` in that list is the previous value. Then post one comment
and no more than one, in exactly this shape, so the next Run can read it too:

```bash
jira-as collaborate comment add <key> -b 'Still firing. value=<current> (previous value=<previous>, <up|down|unchanged>). Open for <duration>.'
```

`<duration>` is how long the Incident has been open: the Jira clock now, minus
the Incident's own `created`. Read both off Jira, never off the Alert — Grafana's
clock and Jira's are not the same clock, and a Notification replayed from a
fixture can carry a `startsAt` that has not happened yet:

```bash
jira-as -o json api call getServerInfo
jira-as issue get <key> -o json
```

`serverTime` from the first, `created` from the second. Write the difference like
`4m30s`. That is the only clock you can reach, so use it for every duration.

If the Match is in `Open`, move it on after commenting — see
[transitions](#moving-an-incident). If it is already in `Work in progress`, stop
here: a repeat is idempotent apart from its comment.

## Step 2c — close the Incident

Count the Firings: every comment on the Incident carrying a `value=` is one, the
opening one included. The duration is the Jira clock now minus the Incident's
`created`, read the same way as in [step 2b](#step-2b--comment-the-trend).

```bash
jira-as collaborate comment add <key> -b 'Resolved after <duration>, <n> Firings. value=<current>. Completed automatically from the Grafana Alert.'
```

Then move it to `Completed` **with a resolution**:

```bash
jira-as lifecycle transition <key> --id <id> --resolution Done
```

Without the resolution the Incident stays in the Incidents queue forever, because
that queue is `resolution = Unresolved`. This is the one place a resolution is set.

## Moving an Incident

Transition names are not status names on this workflow: `Investigate` leads to
`Work in progress` and `Resolve` leads to `Completed`. So never pass `--to`. Read
the transitions off the issue itself and use the id of the one whose `to.name` is
the status you want:

```bash
jira-as lifecycle transitions <key> -o json
jira-as lifecycle transition <key> --id <id>
```

Read them every time. An id that was right last week is not a fact about this issue.

## Finish

End with one line per Alert, naming the Fingerprint, the Incident key and what
changed — `created`, `commented`, `commented and moved to Work in progress`,
`completed`, or `skipped` and why. Nothing else after those lines.
